Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
909 AM EDT Thu Sep 24 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 909 AM EDT Thursday...

Frost advisory has been cancelled.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 230 AM EDT Thursday...

1. Dry weather with seasonable temperatures will continue 
through Friday. 

2. Although exact details are still uncertain, confidence that 
we'll see periods of rain over the weekend has increased, especially 
in southern and eastern Vermont.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 230 AM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: We're in for a couple more pleasant fall days before 
rainier conditions arrive over the weekend. In the meantime, high 
pressure will dominate our weather, keeping the weather dry through 
the rest of the work week. Dense valley fog will dissipate by mid 
morning or so, giving way to another afternoon with ample sunshine 
and highs in the 60s. 

Low pressure off the Mid Atlantic coast will start to make its slow 
push northward tonight and Friday. While rain will remain well to 
our south, mid/high clouds will increase tonight and Friday. This 
will help to keep temperatures a little warmer than the past couple 
of nights, limiting frost formation to just portions of the 
Adirondacks and Northeast Kingdom (where the growing season has 
ended). Therefore, don't anticipate any additional Frost Advisories 
tonight, but subsequent shifts will need to watch cloud and 
temperature trends closely. Friday will feature partly cloudy skies 
and highs in the 60s to near 70F. North winds could be a little on 
the breezy side, particularly in the Champlain Valley due to 
funneling.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Precipitation chances continue to increase for the 
weekend with this forecast package as deterministic and ensemble 
guidance continue to come into better agreement in bringing a 
developing low up along the East Coast on Saturday. The system then 
looks to meander around off the New England coast for a bit before 
finally shunting off to the east. While model consensus is on this 
overall pattern, exactly how far north/west the low approaches and 
how strong it becomes is still uncertain at this time. As noted by 
the previous forecaster, there remains considerable spread in 
potential QPF amounts; the 25th percentile vs 75th percentile range 
is 0-0.44in at BTV; 0.04-0.82in at MPV, and 0.13-1.50in at VSF (for 
48-hr totals ending at 8 am Mon). Accordingly, PoPs have come up as 
well, particularly in southeast VT where 6-hr PoPs top 70% Sunday 
morning. There's still some uncertainty when/where bands of rain 
will rotate back into our region, but expect there will be waves of 
showers through the weekend. 

This system will also bring gusty winds to the region this weekend. 
The NAM, in particular, shows a strong jet wrapping around this 
system, with 70-80kt at 850mb over/just off the MA/RI shore. This 
jet weakens some as it pushes inland toward our area, but guidance 
still indicates 50+ kt 850mb jet spreading over eastern and 
southern VT during the day Saturday. The GFS' winds are weaker, 
with 35-45 kt at 850mb, but either way, breezy conditions are 
looking likely over the weekend, especially over the higher 
terrain and on Lake Champlain. Temperatures will be cool as 
well; some places may struggle to get into the 60s during the 
day, especially in eastern/central VT. Anyone who has outdoor 
plans this weekend should stay tuned for updates and perhaps 
have a backup plan in place should the forecast continue to 
trend toward poor weather.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Through 12Z Friday...Outside of patchy valley fog, VFR conditions
will prevail through the entire TAF period with skies remaining SKC.
Periods of IFR/LIFR conditions are expected briefly this
morning, and then again after 07z Fri in patchy fog in the 
climatologically favored river valleys, including SLK/EFK/MPV 
terminals. Winds remain light and variable through the entire 
forecast period.
